text: Error-prone PCR often substitutes Mn2+ for Mg2+ to destabilize Watson-Crick base pairing and reduce polymerase fidelity, introducing random point mutations across the amplified gene.
explanation: This is true: using Mn2+ instead of Mg2+ is a standard way to lower the fidelity of Taq or similar polymerases, along with imbalanced dNTP concentrations or dedicated low-fidelity polymerases such as Mutazyme II, in order to generate a library of randomly mutated gene variants. Mutation rate is typically tuned to about 1-3 amino acid changes per gene so that most variants remain foldable and testable.
